TEXT.English: Control at least two cities in the Korean core, with no foreign cities there, by 1000 AD.
TEXT.French: Control at least two cities in the Korean core, with no foreign cities there, by 1000 AD.
TEXT.German: Kontrolliert bis 1000 n. Chr. mindestens zwei Städte im koreanischen Kernland, ohne fremde Städte dort.

TEXT.German: Errichtet bis 1600 n. Chr. zwei Seowon.

TEXT.English: Lose no city to conquest before 1900 AD; in 1900, be independent and control at least two cities in the Korean core.

TEXT.English: Hwacha replaces the Catapult; Seowon replaces the University.
TEXT.French: Hwacha replaces the Catapult; Seowon replaces the University.
TEXT.German: Hwacha ersetzt das Katapult; Seowon ersetzt die Universitaet.
TEXT.Italian: Hwacha replaces the Catapult; Seowon replaces the University.
TEXT.Spanish: Hwacha replaces the Catapult; Seowon replaces the University.

TEXT.English: Your chiefdom rises in the Korean peninsula around 800 BC. Develop your northern capital, settle the south, and connect your food and copper. Trade across the seas with Japan while defending the mainland frontier. Bronze Age chiefdoms are represented collectively; a unified kingdom is not assumed.
TEXT.French: Your chiefdom rises in the Korean peninsula around 800 BC. Develop your northern capital, settle the south, and connect your food and copper. Trade across the seas with Japan while defending the mainland frontier. Bronze Age chiefdoms are represented collectively; a unified kingdom is not assumed.
TEXT.German: Euer Stammesgebiet entsteht um 800 v. Chr. auf der koreanischen Halbinsel. Entwickelt die Hauptstadt im Norden, besiedelt den Süden und erschließt Nahrung und Kupfer. Treibt Seehandel mit Japan und sichert die Grenze zum Festland. Die bronzezeitlichen Stammesgebiete werden gemeinsam dargestellt.

TEXT.English: 600 AD: The Three Kingdoms contend for the peninsula. Yeongyang represents Goguryeo, with Pyongyang as your capital. Gyeongju represents the southern kingdoms in this compressed Korean slot. Develop both regional centers and defend against continental invasion; this is a regional aggregation, not a claim of unification in 600.

Gyeongju represents the southern kingdoms in this compressed Korean slot. Develop both regional centers and defend against continental invasion; this is a regional aggregation, not a claim of unification in 600.
TEXT.German: 600 n. Chr.: Die Drei Königreiche ringen um die Halbinsel. Yeongyang vertritt Goguryeo mit der Hauptstadt Pyongyang. Gyeongju steht im gemeinsamen koreanischen Spielerplatz fuer die südlichen Königreiche. Entwickelt beide Zentren und sichert die Festlandsgrenze; Korea ist historisch noch nicht geeint.

TEXT.English: 900 AD: Hyogong rules declining Silla from Gyeongju. Korea is entering the Later Three Kingdoms period; your two cities aggregate regional Korean powers rather than depict a unified monarchy. Strengthen coastal trade and scholarship while preserving independence from the mainland.
TEXT.French: 900 AD: Hyogong rules declining Silla from Gyeongju. Korea is entering the Later Three Kingdoms period; your two cities aggregate regional Korean powers rather than depict a unified monarchy. Strengthen coastal trade and scholarship while preserving independence from the mainland.
TEXT.German: 900 n. Chr.: Hyogong regiert das zerfallende Silla von Gyeongju aus. Korea tritt in die Zeit der Späten Drei Königreiche ein. Die beiden Städte fassen regionale Maechte zusammen. Stärkt Seehandel und Gelehrsamkeit und bewahrt eure Unabhängigkeit.

TEXT.English: 1453 AD: Danjong sits on the Joseon throne in Hanseong. Develop your Seowon, use Hwacha to support the army, and secure the northern frontier at Uiju. Your compact coastal realm can prosper through scholarship and trade without extensive continental conquest.
TEXT.French: 1453 AD: Danjong sits on the Joseon throne in Hanseong. Develop your Seowon, use Hwacha to support the army, and secure the northern frontier at Uiju. Your compact coastal realm can prosper through scholarship and trade without extensive continental conquest.
